outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: None that are merely cosmetic—this task explicitly requires preserving displayed dates and format labels exactly, so deviations are not minor.

Critical issues:
1) Author is reported incorrectly relative to what is shown in the provided DOM evidence. The page heading/title show “Jane Austen,” but the agent output says “Austen, Jane, 1775-1817.” Even if that bibliographic form might exist elsewhere on Gutenberg, it is not what’s evidenced as displayed here, and the task requires reporting what the Gutenberg page shows.
2) Plain Text (accessible) availability is wrong. DOM-model state 0 explicitly includes a link labeled exactly “Plain Text (accessible),” but the agent claimed it was “not visible / not listed.” This is a direct contradiction and fails a core deliverable.
3) Download HTML (zip) availability is not properly verified. The agent asserted it was “not visible / not listed,” but the DOM evidence does not show that the agent actually inspected the full formats list; the label is not present in the provided snapshots, so a definitive “not listed” claim is unsupported.
4) Language: English is not supported by the provided DOM snapshots (no explicit “Language” row is shown). Given the task requires reporting the language field from the Gutenberg page, the agent’s language value is effectively unverified in this run.

What the agent got right: It did access the correct eBook 1342 page. Release Date “Jun 1, 1998” and Last Update “Sep 1, 2026” match the labeled values shown in DOM-model state 1. EPUB3 availability is supported by DOM-model state 0.

Overall outcome: Because at least one required metadata field (author) is wrong per evidence and at least one required format availability (Plain Text (accessible)) is incorrectly reported (contradicted by DOM), the agent did not successfully complete the user’s request.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to open Project Gutenberg eBook #1342 (Pride and Prejudice) and accurately transcribe four on-page metadata fields (author, Release Date, Last Update, language) plus whether three specific download format labels (EPUB3, Plain Text (accessible), Download HTML (zip)) are available—without downloading anything. A reasonable user would not be flexible on incorrect/made-up metadata, or incorrectly claiming a named format is unavailable when it is actually present; they would be flexible only on truly cosmetic formatting that preserves the exact displayed labels/values.
